title: The released Cook 2025 class table has undirected P. pacificus synapse counts; a directed rebuild changes the conserved nerve-ring wiring, and conservation does not predict C. elegans responses
abstract: Question: which nerve-ring connections did Pristionchus pacificus and Caenorhabditis elegans keep, and do kept connections carry more measured signals in C. elegans? We used the public data of Cook et al. 2025 (repository commit 379361a) and the Randi et al. 2023 signal propagation atlas. Finding 1: in the released class table fullsynapses_sjc.csv, the P. pacificus counts are not directed. All P. pacificus counts are on pairs whose presynaptic name comes first in alphabetical order (C. elegans: 51 to 57 percent), and each value is the sum of both directions. The cause is one line in notebook cell 5 that sorts P. pacificus pair names; the same line for C. elegans is commented out. We rebuilt the table with the notebook's own steps without that line; a re-sort of the rebuild gives the released values exactly. Finding 2: with directed counts, core class pairs (synapses in all 12 maps) increase from 65 to 111 and C. elegans-specific pairs decrease from 110 to 37. Of 187 edges present in all 10 C. elegans maps, 80 percent (not 41 percent) have P. pacificus synapses. P. pacificus reciprocity is 0.46 and 0.23, not 0 as in the released table, and inside the C. elegans range. The paper's Fig. 3 statements use a correct directed table and agree with our recount. Finding 3: in neuron-level tests against the atlas, kept connections did not have more detected responses (odds ratio 0.82, 95 percent class bootstrap 0.25 to 2.39) and new P. pacificus wires did not mark C. elegans coupling (1.06, 0.12 to 2.55). An exploratory lead of an earlier campaign result (core versus C. elegans-specific pairs) falls from odds ratio 1.55 to 1.02 with corrected labels. Limitations: two P. pacificus animals of unequal depth, sparse atlas detections with low power, and no rerun of the paper's figures. Code, plan, aggregate results and a retrieval script are included; source data are not bundled.
